title: October jobs report: 165,000 jobs added, unemployment at 4.1%
h1: U.S. employers added 165,000 jobs in October, far more than forecast, and unemployment slipped to 4.1%
description: The October 2026 jobs report, released November 6, showed 165,000 new payroll jobs, 4.1% unemployment and 84,000 jobs in upward revisions to prior months.
standfirst: Hiring in October came in well above what economists expected, and earlier months were revised higher. The stronger numbers add to expectations that the Federal Reserve could raise rates in December.
keywords: October 2026 jobs report, nonfarm payrolls October 2026, unemployment rate 4.1%, BLS employment situation, Fed December rate hike
takeaways: Payrolls grew by 165,000 in October 2026, against a FactSet consensus of 65,000.
Unemployment edged down to 4.1% from 4.2%; August and September were revised up by 84,000 combined.
Futures traders priced about a 77% chance of a Fed rate hike at the December 8 to 9 meeting.
body: The U.S. economy added 165,000 nonfarm payroll jobs in October, the Bureau of Labor Statistics said Friday, November 6, in its Employment Situation report. That is far above the 48,000 average monthly gain of the previous year. Economists surveyed by FactSet had looked for about 65,000, CBS News reported.

Professional and business services led with 70,000 new positions, according to the BLS. Health care added 42,000, transportation and warehousing 25,000 and manufacturing 19,000. Retail, construction and government were roughly flat.

The unemployment rate dipped to 4.1% from 4.2%, leaving about 7.1 million people out of work. The agency also raised its estimates for earlier months: August is now +186,000 and September +60,000, a combined 84,000 more than first reported. Average hourly pay for private workers rose 14 cents in the month to $38.00, a 3.1% gain from a year earlier.
Not every measure improved. CBS News noted that the share of unemployed people who have been looking for work 27 weeks or longer rose to 27.6% from 27.1%.

The Federal Reserve left rates unchanged in October, but inflation sped up in September and remains above the central bank's 2% goal. After the report, CME FedWatch data showed traders putting roughly 77% odds on a rate increase at the December 8 to 9 meeting, according to CBS. Olu Sonola, head of U.S. economics at Fitch Ratings, said the labor market's resilience "keeps the Fed focused on inflation," the network reported.

The November jobs report is the next major labor reading, and the Fed's December decision will show whether policymakers act on the stronger hiring. Our earlier coverage explains what the September rate hike meant for small businesses.

faq.a: Nonfarm payrolls rose by 165,000, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics report released November 6, 2026.

faq.a: It was 4.1%, down slightly from 4.2% in September.
